title: Japanese Foundations: Pre-A1 to A1
summary: An open, milestone-based beginner course for reading, listening, interacting, typing, and writing Japanese in concrete daily-life scenes.
audience: English-speaking teens and adults beginning Japanese on phone, tablet, and web.

units.title: Writing Systems
units.summary: Hear Japanese rhythm and see how hiragana, katakana, and kanji work together before tracing their shapes.

units.title: Read And Write Hiragana
units.summary: Learn the complete 46-character hiragana map in small sound groups with immediate recall and cumulative review.

units.title: Hiragana Sound Tools
units.summary: Decode dakuten, handakuten, small kana, doubled consonants, contracted sounds, long vowels, and moraic ん.

units.title: Read And Write Katakana
units.summary: Transfer the hiragana sound map to all 46 basic katakana, look-alikes, long vowels, and common loanwords.

units.title: Romaji And Kana Input
units.summary: Separate Japanese spelling, pronunciation, learner romanization, and the keys an IME needs.

units.title: First Connections
units.summary: Exchange greetings, identify people and things, understand basic time, talk about family and likes, and order simply.

units.title: Everyday Navigator
units.summary: Navigate places, routines, transport, invitations, requests, shopping, signs, and short messages.

units.title: Starter Kanji In Context
units.summary: Read, trace, recall, and use beginner kanji through vocabulary, signs, messages, and short sentences.

skills.label: Kana sounds and rhythm
skills.description: Hear mora rhythm and distinguish the core kana sound patterns.

skills.label: Kana recognition
skills.description: Recognize hiragana and katakana in words, signs, and tiny texts.

skills.label: Kana handwriting
skills.description: Trace and recall textbook-style kana with the intended stroke order.

skills.label: Kana learning interaction
skills.description: Use kana knowledge to ask, answer, and clarify a simple reading or input question.

skills.label: Japanese keyboard input
skills.description: Choose IME keys separately from learner-facing pronunciation and romanization.

skills.label: A1 listening
skills.description: Understand familiar words and short, slowly delivered everyday exchanges.

skills.label: A1 reading
skills.description: Find concrete information in short sentences, signs, messages, and mini-readers.

skills.label: A1 interaction
skills.description: Exchange basic personal information and complete predictable everyday tasks.

skills.label: A1 writing
skills.description: Write familiar characters and create a very short personal or practical message.

stages.label: Kana Explorer
stages.summary: Build a reliable sound-to-symbol foundation across recognition, reading, handwriting, and keyboard input.

outcomes.statement: I can hear and tap the mora rhythm of a short familiar kana word.
I can recognize the 46 basic hiragana and katakana in standard order.
I can write a sampled basic kana character from memory using its stroke order.
I can explain a simple difference between a particle's sound and its IME spelling.
I can type particles, small kana, doubled consonants, and long vowels with an IME.

stages.label: First Connections
stages.summary: Use short rehearsed language to meet someone, exchange concrete information, express preferences, and order.

outcomes.statement: I can understand a slowly spoken name, age, time, or simple preference.
I can understand the main details in a short greeting or café scene.
I can write a two-sentence introduction with my name and one personal fact.
I can greet someone, give my name, ask one basic question, and respond politely.

stages.label: Everyday Navigator
stages.summary: Complete predictable daily tasks involving places, routines, transport, requests, purchases, signs, and messages.

outcomes.statement: I can understand the time, place, and transport in a short familiar plan.
I can locate a concrete time, place, price, or instruction in a short text.
I can write a short message giving a meeting time and place.
I can ask directions, make a request, arrange a meeting, or buy a simple item.
